title: ForeSight-HF, a GPT-5 mini decision-support tool, scores two nursing-home heart-failure cases; patients managed independently
summary: Mount Sinai authors report that ForeSight-HF (GPT-5 mini on ProviderLoop) generated diuresis advice for a warm/wet and de-escalation advice for a cold/dry nursing-home patient; neither guided care.
account: Glajchen and colleagues describe ForeSight-HF in JACC: Case Reports. The tool uses GPT-5 mini to produce heart-failure assessments and treatment suggestions from nursing-facility notes. The paper states that the authors accessed GPT-5 mini in late 2025. It presents two illustrative cases and states explicitly that the tool's outputs did not guide clinical care. Both patients were managed independently of the system for four months. In the second case, the clinicians’ diuretic and medication decisions differed from the AI recommendations. The proposed workflow includes weekly physician review. The paper gives no evidence that the model directed these patients’ treatment. ProviderLoop supplied the platform, and senior author Jeffrey Bander disclosed that he founded and owned it. The patients’ clinical outcomes cannot be attributed to the AI. The journal received the manuscript on 6 March 2026 and published it online on 3 June 2026. At Mass General Brigham, a separate team piloted GPT-5.2 heart-failure therapy recommendations in early 2026. Helseth and colleagues reported on 29 August 2026 that at least one recommendation was implemented at 13 of 56 visits (23%), with no control group. As of 29 October 2026, Europe PMC listed no trial, follow-up report or citing article on ForeSight-HF.

fields.account: Glajchen and colleagues describe ForeSight-HF in JACC: Case Reports. The tool uses GPT-5 mini to produce heart-failure assessments and treatment suggestions from nursing-facility notes. The paper states that the authors accessed GPT-5 mini in late 2025. It presents two illustrative cases and states explicitly that the tool's outputs did not guide clinical care. Both patients were managed independently of the system for four months. In the second case, the clinicians’ diuretic and medication decisions differed from the AI recommendations. The proposed workflow includes weekly physician review. The paper gives no evidence that the model directed these patients’ treatment. ProviderLoop supplied the platform, and senior author Jeffrey Bander disclosed that he founded and owned it. The patients’ clinical outcomes cannot be attributed to the AI. The journal received the manuscript on 6 March 2026 and published it online on 3 June 2026. At Mass General Brigham, a separate team piloted GPT-5.2 heart-failure therapy recommendations in early 2026. Helseth and colleagues reported on 29 August 2026 that at least one recommendation was implemented at 13 of 56 visits (23%), with no control group. As of 29 October 2026, Europe PMC listed no trial, follow-up report or citing article on ForeSight-HF.

echoes.setting: Mass General Brigham outpatient cardiology, Boston: the team identified 1,016 eligible heart-failure patients with cardiology return visits scheduled from January to March 2026 and used GPT-5.2 to draft therapy recommendations from the health record; in a six-week pilot, six clinicians received them by message (Helseth et al., J Card Fail, 29 August 2026). The authors report that the recommendations were safe and feasible to deliver and that at least one recommendation was implemented at 13 of 56 visits (23%), with no control group.
